This session is recorded by Entire and published: work only inside this repository and never mention anything outside it. Run every command in the foreground and wait for it (no background commands; use long timeouts). Do not git commit or push. Memory is limited: one library at a time.

Secrets: the environment has TRUEUP_MODEL_KEY, TRUEUP_MODEL_BASE_URL, NEATLOGS_API_KEY and NEATLOGS_PROJECT. Never print, log, echo or write their values anywhere (not even partly). Check only whether they are set.

Task 1: the model client and the planner.
- `src/trueup/model.py`: one client using the `openai` SDK against TRUEUP_MODEL_BASE_URL (an OpenAI-compatible LiteLLM proxy). Models: `claude-sonnet-4.6` for planning and fixing, `claude-haiku` for cheap jobs. Never use any opus model. Retries with backoff on errors; invalid JSON from the model -> retry, then stop that worker with a clear error.
- Spending guard: before every model call, GET `<base without /v1>/key/info` with the key as Bearer and read `info.spend`; refuse to call if spend >= 15.0 (USD) and stop with a clear message. Record spend before/after each run in the run directory. Unit-test the guard with a fake HTTP response.
- Planner (`src/trueup/planner.py`): reads a tracing library's wrapper source (from its installed venv), the scenario library and the current findings, and proposes NEW scenarios as JSON data only (never code), each naming the expected truth in fields the comparer can check. Code validates every proposal against the scenario schema and the fake's supported behaviours; invalid ones are rejected with the reason and counted. At most 2 revision tries per rejected proposal (send the rejection reason back). Accepted proposals go to `scenarios/proposed/<lib>/` and can be swept with `trueup sweep <lib> --proposed`.
- CLI: `trueup plan <lib> [--max N]` (default N=5).

Task 2: trace Trueup itself with neatlogs.
- Add `neatlogs` as a dependency. At the start of every trueup command that calls the model (plan now, fix later): neatlogs.init with the API key from the environment, the openai instrumentation, and tags (run id, library, trueup version). One trueup run = one neatlogs session. Each worker gets its own workflow name (`trueup-planner`, `trueup-runner`, `trueup-comparer`, `trueup-checker`, `trueup-deduper`) and custom attributes `trueup.run_id`, `trueup.library`, `trueup.verdict` where it applies. Flush on exit, including on a crash (test this). If NEATLOGS_API_KEY is not set, run without it and say so once. IMPORTANT: this outer tracing must not interfere with the inner per-scenario capture, which runs in separate subprocesses with export disabled; keep it that way and test that the inner spans never leave the machine.
- `trueup doctor` reports whether neatlogs and the model are reachable (one cheap GET each; no model call).

Then actually run `trueup plan openllmetry --max 3` and `trueup plan neatlogs --max 3` once each (real model calls; keep total cost low), sweep the accepted proposals, and run the checker on any lead they produce. Record in hackathon.md: proposals made, accepted, rejected with reasons, leads and findings from them, model tokens and cost (from the key's spend), and the neatlogs session ids (not URLs with secrets). Be honest if the planner found nothing new.

Update CHANGELOG.md and README status. Plain words, no filler. `uv run pytest -q` must pass. Finish with a summary.

Trueup finds where your AI agent's traces disagree with what really happened, fixes the tracing code, and proves the fix.

## What it does

Teams watch their AI agents through tracing libraries such as neatlogs, OpenInference and OpenLLMetry. These libraries wrap the AI provider's SDK and record each call. When a wrapper gets a case wrong, the dashboard can show a crashed run as OK, miss a refusal, or show twice the real cost.

Trueup runs the agent against a fake provider, so it knows what really happened. It captures what the trace says and compares the two. When they disagree, it looks for the cause in the tracing library, writes a fix with a test, and checks that the fix works.

The work is split into small workers: planner, runner, comparer, checker, deduper, fixer, verifier and reporter. A language model proposes; plain code decides.

## Status: early build

`trueup doctor`, `trueup sweep <neatlogs|openinference|openllmetry>`, `trueup audit <script> --library <lib>` and `trueup check <run_id|latest> --library <lib>` work.

`sweep` runs the scenarios (plain SDK, LangChain/LangGraph and the OpenAI Agents SDK; pick with `--framework`) against a fake provider, compares truth with the trace, prints a table of leads and writes truth, trace and `leads.json` to `.trueup/runs/<run_id>/`. A lead is a disagreement between truth and trace; it is not a confirmed bug.

`audit` runs your script's `main()` against the fake (through `OPENAI_BASE_URL` / `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL`) under the chosen library, once per fake scenario on each provider route the script calls, and compares the same way. It needs a `main()` with no arguments that uses the `openai` or `anthropic` SDK; see `src/trueup/audit.py` for its limits.

`check` runs the checker over a sweep's leads. A lead becomes a finding only if it reproduces twice in fresh processes, on the recommended setup, on the latest release and on the library's main branch, the fake really sent what truth says, the harness is sane, another library or the OpenTelemetry conventions show the right behaviour, and a repro under 40 lines shows it. Otherwise it is withdrawn with the rule that failed (kept and counted). Findings that share a cause are grouped, then searched for in the library's GitHub issues and PRs (read only). It writes `findings.json` and `withdrawn.json` in the run dir.

The other commands (`fix`, `upstream`, `verify`, `report`) print "not built yet" and exit 2.

Exit codes: 0 no leads, 1 leads found, 2 could not run.

## Run it

Needs Python 3.12 and [uv](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/).

```sh
uv sync
uv run trueup doctor
uv run pytest -q         # offline unit tests
uv run pytest -q -m e2e  # builds per-library venvs, runs subprocesses
uv run trueup sweep neatlogs
uv run trueup sweep openllmetry --framework openai-agents
uv run trueup audit examples/agent.py --library openinference
uv run trueup check latest --library neatlogs
```

# Build log

neatHack, 10-12 Oct 2026.

## 2026-10-10: skeleton

- Set up the uv project (Python 3.12, src layout) with the `trueup` command.
- Added the data model in `trueup.core`: Observation, Mismatch, Run, Finding and Severity, each with `to_dict`/`from_dict`.
- `trueup doctor` reports the Python version and whether the two keys are set, without printing them. Other commands exit 2 with "not built yet".
- Tests for the round trip, severity order and doctor. CI runs them on push.
- Nothing is audited yet. No findings so far.

## 2026-10-10: the truth side

- `trueup.fake`: a local fake provider (stdlib http.server in a thread, random free port). It speaks OpenAI Chat Completions, OpenAI Responses and Anthropic Messages. The request's model name picks the scenario: plain, streamed with and without usage, two parallel tool calls with split streamed arguments, refusal, n=2, HTTP 500 and 529, error event mid-stream, status failed and incomplete, reasoning summary, thinking, tool_use with input_json_delta, and a dropped connection. Every id is unique per call and per fake instance. The truth log records each request and what was sent back, including tokens per call, or that no usage was sent.
- 34 fixture tests run the real `openai` and `anthropic` SDKs against the fake. Two SDK behaviours we found and recorded: the openai SDK passes a Responses `error` event to the app instead of raising, and the anthropic SDK lets a dropped stream through as a raw `RemoteProtocolError`, not an SDK exception.
- `trueup.scenarios`: 31 plain-SDK scenarios as data (chat 12, Responses 9, Anthropic 10), each with expected truth. A unit test runs every app with no tracing library and checks the expectations against what really happens. That check caught one wrong expectation (streamed tool calls without include_usage carry no tokens). 20 LangChain/LangGraph/OpenAI Agents cases are listed as not_built.
- `trueup.runner`: runs one scenario in a fresh subprocess in `.trueup/venvs/<lib>` (built with uv), using the library's recommended setup and an in-memory span exporter. It returns truth plus spans as JSON. A scenario that cannot run is reported NOT RUN with the reason.
- Regression tests for four traps: reused response ids, a reused async client across asyncio.run, a missing-usage reply read as a bug, and neatlogs exporting to a dead endpoint.
- `trueup sweep <library>` writes observations and `summary.txt` to `.trueup/runs/<run_id>/`. All three libraries ran 31/31. The first openllmetry sweep was 0/31 NOT RUN because `traceloop-sdk` imports `httpx` without declaring it; we now install `httpx` in that venv.
- Leads for the comparer (not judged yet): neatlogs adds `stream_options.include_usage` to the app's streamed chat request. openinference exports no span for a stream closed early, or for a Responses stream that ends with an error event. openllmetry marks chat streams that raised (error event, cut) as OK, and exports no span for Responses failed/incomplete or for Anthropic stream errors and cuts.

## 2026-10-10: the comparer and the reports

- `trueup.core.compare` checks truth against the spans: run status, call status, call count, span closed, tokens, output (text, refusal, tool calls with arguments compared as JSON), finish, plus a "request changed" note. Severity: HIGH changes a number or status a dashboard shows by default, MEDIUM is wrong or missing span detail, LOW is extra or cosmetic.
- `trueup.core.adapters`: one data-driven adapter per library saying where it keeps tokens, finish reasons, outputs and response ids. Tested against span JSON from the sweeps, saved in `tests/fixtures/spans/` with stack traces and local URLs removed. OpenLLMetry error spans for failed Responses streams have no `gen_ai.operation.name`, so its adapter keys on `gen_ai.provider.name`.
- Choices made while comparing: finish reasons are compared through a synonym table (end_turn = stop, tool_use = tool_calls = tool_call, incomplete = length), because OpenLLMetry normalises them; a completed Responses call that asked for a tool may show `tool_call`. When the app closes a stream early, output, tokens and finish are not compared, since the app never got them. Tokens are only compared when the fake sent usage. Spans are matched to calls by response id, then by start order.
- A mismatch is called a lead. `trueup sweep <lib>` now prints a leads table, writes `leads.json` and exits 1 if there is any lead.
- `trueup audit <agent.py> --library <lib>` runs the script's `main()` against the fake, once per fake scenario on each route the script calls, and compares. Limits are written in `src/trueup/audit.py`. Tried on `examples/agent.py` under openinference: 8 runs, 1 lead (refusal not recorded).

Sweeps after the comparer (31/31 ran for each library). These are leads, not confirmed bugs; the self-check comes next.

| library | leads | high | medium | low | notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| neatlogs | 22 | 4 | 18 | 0 | 5 |
| openinference | 10 | 2 | 8 | 0 | 0 |
| openllmetry | 14 | 11 | 3 | 0 | 0 |

Leads per check:

| check | neatlogs | openinference | openllmetry |
|---|---|---|---|
| run_status | 1 | 0 | 3 |
| call_status | 1 | 0 | 3 |
| call_count | 0 | 0 | 0 |
| span_closed | 0 | 2 | 4 |
| tokens | 3 | 0 | 4 |
| output | 7 | 1 | 0 |
| finish | 10 | 7 | 0 |

- neatlogs: Anthropic `messages.stream` spans carry no tokens, text, tool calls or finish reason (3 scenarios); Responses spans carry no status/finish (7) and no function calls (2); the chat refusal is not recorded; the Responses stream that ends with an error event stays UNSET with no exception event. The 5 notes are neatlogs adding `stream_options.include_usage` to streamed chat requests; tokens were compared against what the fake really sent.
- openinference: no span for a chat stream closed early or for a Responses stream ending in an error event; Responses spans carry no status/finish (7); the chat refusal is not recorded.
- openllmetry: chat streams that raised (error event, cut) and the Responses error-event stream end OK; no span for Responses failed/incomplete or for Anthropic stream error/cut; Anthropic streamed spans record 4 output tokens where the provider sent 3 (4 scenarios).

## 2026-10-10: framework scenarios

- The fake now runs agent flows. It picks each reply from the request, so it keeps no state: no tool result yet means a tool call, a tool result means the answer. Chat Completions: one tool, two parallel tools, a loop that always asks for the tool, and HTTP 500 on the second call. Responses (for the OpenAI Agents SDK): one tool, a loop, 500 on the second call, a tool name the agent does not have, and an error event or a dropped connection in the streamed answer, after the full streamed event sequence of the first call. Fixture tests run them through the real openai SDK, LangChain, LangGraph and the Agents SDK.
- 20 framework scenarios are built: LangChain 6, LangGraph 6, OpenAI Agents SDK 8. Each has expected truth, including which tools really ran and which raised. The untraced check runs all 51 scenarios with the real SDKs. Two things it showed: LangGraph's `create_react_agent` does not raise at the step limit (it answers "Sorry, need more steps"), and langchain-openai raises its own `OpenAIAPIError` and `OpenAIConnectionError`.
- Setups per framework. neatlogs: `neatlogs.init(instrumentations=[...])` with its README keys (`langchain`, `langchain`+`langgraph`, `openai_agents`), export off. OpenInference: `LangChainInstrumentor` or `OpenAIAgentsInstrumentor`, and the OpenAI/Anthropic ones only for plain SDK runs. OpenLLMetry: `Traceloop.init(exporter=<in-memory>, disable_batch=True)` for everything. The Agents SDK's own uploader to api.openai.com is removed; the instrumentors' processors stay. Each agent gets its own AsyncOpenAI client.
- Trap found: the first neatlogs LangChain run exported no spans and raised no error. neatlogs checks `import langchain`, and the venv had `langchain-core` and `langchain-openai` but not `langchain`, so it logged "Skipped: langchain (not installed)". Every venv now installs `langchain`. Before a framework scenario runs, the runner checks that the framework imports and that an instrumentor for it is active, and reports NOT RUN with the reason if not. A regression test covers this.
- Comparer: run status uses the trace root (for the Agents SDK, "Agent workflow"). Two new checks. `tools`: every tool that really ran has a tool span, and a tool that raised has an ERROR span or an exception event. `error_recorded`: when the app raised but no provider call failed (unknown tool, max turns), some span must record an error. The OpenLLMetry adapter no longer counts LangGraph task, tool, agent and workflow spans as LLM calls. A scenario can say the app itself asked for stream usage, so LangChain's `stream_usage=True` is not reported as the library changing the request.

Sweeps with all 51 scenarios (runs `20261010T203332Z-neatlogs`, `20261010T203600Z-openinference`, `20261010T203755Z-openllmetry`). 51/51 ran for each library; nothing NOT RUN. The plain-SDK counts are unchanged from the last sweep. These are leads, not confirmed bugs.

| library | leads | high | medium | low | notes | of which framework |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| neatlogs | 58 | 9 | 49 | 0 | 5 | 36 (high 5, medium 31) |
| openinference | 19 | 7 | 12 | 0 | 0 | 9 (high 5, medium 4) |
| openllmetry | 29 | 21 | 8 | 0 | 0 | 15 (high 10, medium 5) |

Leads per check (all scenarios; framework scenarios in brackets):

| check | neatlogs | openinference | openllmetry |
|---|---|---|---|
| run_status | 6 (5) | 5 (5) | 8 (5) |
| call_status | 4 (3) | 3 (3) | 6 (3) |
| call_count | 0 | 0 | 5 (5) |
| span_closed | 0 | 2 (0) | 4 (0) |
| tokens | 3 (0) | 0 | 4 (0) |
| output | 8 (1) | 2 (1) | 1 (1) |
| finish | 37 (27) | 7 (0) | 0 |
| tools | 0 | 0 | 0 |
| error_recorded | 0 | 0 | 1 (1) |

- All three: when an Agents SDK run raises (500 on the second call, max turns, unknown tool, streamed error event, streamed cut), the root "Agent workflow" span is OK (5 scenarios each). For the provider failures the inner `response` span is ERROR but has no exception event (3 each). The LangChain refusal is not recorded as output (1 each). Tool spans were right everywhere, including the raised tool.
- neatlogs: framework LLM spans have no `neatlogs.llm.finish_reason` (27). The OpenInference `llm.finish_reason` is on the same span; the adapter reads the neatlogs namespace only, as in the plain-SDK sweeps.
- openllmetry: in non-streamed Agents SDK runs every model call gets two LLM spans, one from the Agents SDK instrumentation and one from the OpenAI instrumentation under it. That doubles calls and tokens (ag-run: 2 calls and 36 tokens really; 4 spans and 72 tokens in the trace). Streamed runs get one span per call. The unknown-tool error is on no span: `no_such_tool` only appears as the tool call in the model's output.

Answers to the three questions:
1. Does a crashed Agents SDK run show OK at the top level? Yes, in all three libraries, in all 5 crash scenarios.
2. Does OpenLLMetry with Traceloop.init double LLM calls and tokens for the Agents SDK? Yes in non-streamed runs (5 of 5 scenarios, exactly 2x). Streamed runs are not affected (3 of 3 have one span per call and the right tokens).
3. Does an unknown-tool error appear anywhere in the trace? neatlogs and OpenInference: only as the status description of the `turn` span (ERROR, no exception event); the root stays OK. OpenLLMetry: nowhere.

## 2026-10-10: the checker and the deduper

- `trueup check <run_id|latest> --library <lib>` takes a sweep's leads through seven rules: reproduces twice in fresh processes; recommended setup with the framework installed; latest release (checked against PyPI) and the library's main branch (shallow clone, installed into `.trueup/venvs/<lib>-main`); the fake sent what truth claims; harness sane (own client per event loop, export off, no endpoint); another library or the OTel conventions show the right behaviour; a repro under 40 lines reproduces it. A lead that passes every rule is a finding; otherwise it is withdrawn with the failing rule, kept as a lead, or marked "disputed semantics". Withdrawn leads stay in `withdrawn.json`.
- Findings with the same library, check, field and code path are grouped into one finding with a list of scenarios.
- The deduper searches each library's issues and PRs (all states, `gh search issues --include-prs`), lists the integration's titles and records each search with its date (in `findings.json`). Read only: nothing was opened, commented on or posted.
- Repros are generated per scenario in `.trueup/runs/<run>/repros/` (31 lines each). They run offline with fake keys, but they import trueup for the fake provider and the app code, so they are not yet standalone scripts for an upstream issue.

### Trueup's own false alarm: neatlogs finish reason

The neatlogs adapter read the finish reason only from `neatlogs.llm.finish_reason` / `neatlogs.llm.choices.N.finish_reason`. In the real spans from run `20261010T203332Z-neatlogs`, every framework LLM span (LangChain, LangGraph, Agents SDK) comes from an OpenInference instrumentor (scope `openinference.instrumentation.langchain` / `.openai_agents`). These spans carry the right finish reason in `llm.finish_reason`. neatlogs copies tokens and tool calls into its own namespace but not the finish reason. The finish reason is in the exported trace, so the leads were ours. The adapter now also reads `llm.finish_reason`.

Same saved run, compared again: 58 leads before, 31 after. All 27 removed leads were `finish` leads on framework scenarios: ag-bad-tool 1, ag-llm-fails 1, ag-max-turns 3, ag-run 2, ag-streamed 2, ag-streamed-cut 1, ag-streamed-error 1, ag-tool-raises 2, lc-invoke 1, lc-refusal 1, lc-stream 1, lg-agent 2, lg-llm-fails 1, lg-parallel 2, lg-step-limit 3, lg-stream 2, lg-tool-raises 1. The 10 plain-SDK finish leads stay. Whether the neatlogs dashboard shows `llm.finish_reason` was not checked.

### Results

Checked against the latest releases (neatlogs 1.4.26; OpenInference openai 0.1.65, anthropic 3.0.3, langchain 0.1.79, openai-agents 2.5.3; OpenLLMetry 0.62.4, all equal to PyPI) and main (neatlogs `202f8776ea`, openinference `c364180e5b`, openllmetry `df4921a409`). Every main branch installed.

| library | leads | finding leads | findings (grouped) | high | medium | withdrawn | disputed | already known |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| neatlogs | 31 | 27 | 12 | 3 | 9 | 0 | 2 groups (4 leads) | 3 |
| openinference | 19 | 15 | 6 | 3 | 3 | 0 | 2 groups (4 leads) | 0 |
| openllmetry | 29 | 23 | 9 | 6 | 3 | 2 (latest_and_main) | 2 groups (4 leads) | 1 |

Withdrawn: openllmetry, oa-resp-failed and oa-resp-incomplete (no span for a Responses call with status failed or incomplete). Both reproduce on 0.62.4 but not on main, so they are fixed there.

Disputed semantics, in all three libraries: (1) on Agents SDK provider failures the `response` span is ERROR but has no exception event (ag-llm-fails, ag-streamed-error, ag-streamed-cut); the conventions require the status, not the event. (2) the LangChain refusal is not recorded as output (lc-refusal); the GenAI conventions have no refusal part and no library records it.

Both Responses tool-call findings match open PR https://github.com/neatlogs/neatlogs/pull/186 (issue https://github.com/neatlogs/neatlogs/issues/185). From its description, PR 180 also covers the `messages.stream()` tokens, finish and tool-call findings (same cause), but the automated title match only marked the output one.

# Changelog

## Unreleased

- `trueup check <run_id|latest> [--library x]`: runs the checker and the deduper over a sweep's leads and writes `findings.json`, `withdrawn.json` and `evidence.json` next to `leads.json`. Prints findings by severity, withdrawn by rule and already-known. Exits 1 if there is a finding.
- Checker (`trueup.core.checker`): seven rules, each a pure function over recorded evidence: fresh process twice, recommended setup, latest release and main branch, fake truthful, harness sane, reference (another library or the OTel conventions), and a repro under 40 lines. A lead is a finding only if every rule passes; otherwise it is withdrawn with the rule that failed, kept as a lead, or marked "disputed semantics". Withdrawn leads are kept and counted.
- Evidence gathering (`trueup.check`): upgrades the library's venv to the latest release and records versions against PyPI, reruns each scenario twice, builds `.trueup/venvs/<lib>-main` from a shallow clone of the library's main branch, reads the other libraries' latest sweeps, and generates and runs a repro per scenario (`repros/` in the run dir). Leads are compared again with today's adapters.
- Grouping (`trueup.core.group`): leads with the same library, check, field and code path become one finding with a list of scenarios.
- Deduper (`trueup.dedupe`): searches the library's GitHub issues and PRs in all states with `gh search issues --include-prs`, lists the integration's titles, records each search with its date and marks a finding "already known" with the link when a title names the integration and the behaviour. Read only.
- Repro generator (`trueup.core.repro`): a short script that runs a scenario offline under a library and prints its leads.
- Deduper: title matches read by hand that do not cover a finding are kept as "related" with the reason; token findings ignore titles about reasoning tokens.
- Check results are cached per scenario in the run dir (`check-cache/`), so an interrupted check resumes.
- Fix: the neatlogs adapter now also reads `llm.finish_reason`. neatlogs framework spans come from the OpenInference instrumentors and carry the finish reason only there. This removed 27 false finish leads.

- Framework scenarios: 20 built (LangChain 6, LangGraph 6, OpenAI Agents SDK 8), each with expected truth, including which tools ran and which raised. App code in `trueup.runner.framework_apps`.
- Fake provider: agent flows on Chat Completions and Responses. Tool call then answer, parallel tools, a tool loop, 500 on the second call, an unknown tool name, and an error event or a cut in the second streamed call.
- Runner: each library's setup per framework. neatlogs uses its README keys, OpenInference its LangChain and OpenAI Agents instrumentors, OpenLLMetry `Traceloop.init`. The framework packages, `langchain` included, are installed in every venv. A framework scenario is NOT RUN, with the reason, if the framework does not import or no instrumentor for it is active. The Agents SDK's own trace upload is turned off.
- Comparer: run status uses the trace root. New `tools` and `error_recorded` checks. OpenLLMetry framework spans (agent, task, tool, workflow) are no longer counted as LLM calls. A scenario can say the app asked for stream usage itself.
- `trueup sweep <library> --framework all|none|langchain|openai-agents`. The default is all.
- Dev dependencies: `langchain-openai`, `langgraph`, `openai-agents`.

- Comparer (`trueup.core.compare`): checks run status, call status, call count, span closed, tokens, output and finish, with HIGH/MEDIUM/LOW severity. Records a library changing the request (such as adding `stream_options.include_usage`) as a LOW note.
- Adapters (`trueup.core.adapters`): one per library for neatlogs, OpenInference and OpenLLMetry, tested on saved span JSON in `tests/fixtures/spans/`.
- Reports (`trueup.core.report`): leads table and `leads.json`.
- `trueup sweep <library>` compares, prints the leads table, writes `leads.json`, and exits 1 if there is any lead.
- `trueup audit <script> --library <library>`: runs the script's `main()` against the fake through `OPENAI_BASE_URL` / `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL`, once per fake scenario on each route it calls, and compares. Example script in `examples/agent.py`.
- The fake provider can be told which scenario to answer with on a route, whatever the model name.

Trueup finds where your AI agent's traces disagree with what really happened, fixes the tracing code, and proves the fix.

## What it does

Teams watch their AI agents through tracing libraries such as neatlogs, OpenInference and OpenLLMetry. These libraries wrap the AI provider's SDK and record each call. When a wrapper gets a case wrong, the dashboard can show a crashed run as OK, miss a refusal, or show twice the real cost.

Trueup runs the agent against a fake provider, so it knows what really happened. It captures what the trace says and compares the two. When they disagree, it looks for the cause in the tracing library, writes a fix with a test, and checks that the fix works.

The work is split into small workers: planner, runner, comparer, checker, deduper, fixer, verifier and reporter. A language model proposes; plain code decides.

## Status: early build

`trueup doctor`, `trueup sweep <neatlogs|openinference|openllmetry>`, `trueup audit <script> --library <lib>` and `trueup check <run_id|latest> --library <lib>` work.

`sweep` runs the scenarios (plain SDK, LangChain/LangGraph and the OpenAI Agents SDK; pick with `--framework`) against a fake provider, compares truth with the trace, prints a table of leads and writes truth, trace and `leads.json` to `.trueup/runs/<run_id>/`. A lead is a disagreement between truth and trace; it is not a confirmed bug.

`audit` runs your script's `main()` against the fake (through `OPENAI_BASE_URL` / `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL`) under the chosen library, once per fake scenario on each provider route the script calls, and compares the same way. It needs a `main()` with no arguments that uses the `openai` or `anthropic` SDK; see `src/trueup/audit.py` for its limits.

`check` runs the checker over a sweep's leads. A lead becomes a finding only if it reproduces twice in fresh processes, on the recommended setup, on the latest release and on the library's main branch, the fake really sent what truth says, the harness is sane, another library or the OpenTelemetry conventions show the right behaviour, and a repro under 40 lines shows it. Otherwise it is withdrawn with the rule that failed (kept and counted). Findings that share a cause are grouped, then searched for in the library's GitHub issues and PRs (read only). It writes `findings.json` and `withdrawn.json` in the run dir.

The other commands (`fix`, `upstream`, `verify`, `report`) print "not built yet" and exit 2.

Exit codes: 0 no leads, 1 leads found, 2 could not run.

uv run trueup doctor
uv run pytest -q         # offline unit tests
uv run pytest -q -m e2e  # builds per-library venvs, runs subprocesses
uv run trueup sweep neatlogs
uv run trueup sweep openllmetry --framework openai-agents
uv run trueup audit examples/agent.py --library openinference
uv run trueup check latest --library neatlogs

2	
3	## What it does
4	
5	Teams watch their AI agents through tracing libraries such as neatlogs, OpenInference and OpenLLMetry. These libraries wrap the AI provider's SDK and record each call. When a wrapper gets a case wrong, the dashboard can show a crashed run as OK, miss a refusal, or show twice the real cost.
6	
7	Trueup runs the agent against a fake provider, so it knows what really happened. It captures what the trace says and compares the two. When they disagree, it looks for the cause in the tracing library, writes a fix with a test, and checks that the fix works.
8	
9	The work is split into small workers: planner, runner, comparer, checker, deduper, fixer, verifier and reporter. A language model proposes; plain code decides.

"""Command line entry point."""

from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import os
import sys
from pathlib import Path
from typing import Sequence

from trueup.runner.setups import LIBRARIES

# Exit codes
EXIT_OK = 0  # no mismatches
EXIT_MISMATCH = 1  # mismatches found
EXIT_ERROR = 2  # could not run

KEY_VARS = ("NEATLOGS_API_KEY", "TRUEUP_MODEL_KEY")
NOT_BUILT = ("fix", "upstream", "verify", "report")


def doctor() -> int:
    ok = sys.version_info >= (3, 12)
    v = sys.version_info
    print(f"python: {v.major}.{v.minor}.{v.micro} ({'ok' if ok else 'need 3.12+'})")
    for name in KEY_VARS:
        # Only report presence. Never print the value.
        state = "set" if os.environ.get(name) else "not set"
        print(f"{name}: {state}")
    return EXIT_OK if ok else EXIT_ERROR


def build_parser() -> argparse.ArgumentParser:
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(
        prog="trueup",
        description="Find where AI agent traces disagree with what really happened.",
    )
    sub = parser.add_subparsers(dest="command", required=True)
    for name in NOT_BUILT:
        sub.add_parser(name, help="not built yet")
    sub.add_parser("doctor", help="check the local setup")
    sw = sub.add_parser("sweep", help="run the scenarios against one tracing library")
    sw.add_argument("library", choices=LIBRARIES)
    sw.add_argument("--framework", default="all", choices=("all", "none", "langchain", "openai-agents"),
                    help="none: plain SDK; langchain: LangChain and LangGraph; default all")
    au = sub.add_parser("audit", help="run your script's main() against the fake provider and compare its trace")
    au.add_argument("script", type=Path, help="Python file with a main() that calls the openai or anthropic SDK")
    au.add_argument("--library", required=True, choices=LIBRARIES, help="tracing library to set up")
    ck = sub.add_parser("check", help="run the checker and dedupe over a sweep's leads")
    ck.add_argument("run_id", help="a run id under .trueup/runs, or latest")
    ck.add_argument("--library", choices=LIBRARIES, help="with latest: the newest sweep of this library")
    return parser


def main(argv: Sequence[str] | None = None) -> int:
    args = build_parser().parse_args(argv)
    if args.command == "doctor":
        return doctor()
    if args.command == "sweep":
        from trueup.sweep import exit_code, sweep

        _, results = sweep(Path.cwd(), args.library, args.framework)
        return exit_code(results)
    if args.command == "audit":
        from trueup.audit import audit
        from trueup.sweep import exit_code

        _, results = audit(Path.cwd(), args.library, args.script)
        return exit_code(results)
    if args.command == "check":
        from trueup.check import check

        try:
            res = check(Path.cwd(), args.run_id, args.library)
        except (FileNotFoundError, ValueError) as e:
            print(f"trueup check: {e}", file=sys.stderr)
            return EXIT_ERROR
        return EXIT_MISMATCH if res["counts"]["findings"] else EXIT_OK
    print(f"trueup {args.command}: not built yet", file=sys.stderr)
    return EXIT_ERROR


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())

"""The scenario library, as data.

Each scenario names the fake model it calls (the fake picks its behaviour from
the model name), the app code that drives it (`app`, a function in
trueup.runner.apps), and the truth fields we expect the run to produce.

Expected truth keys (only the ones listed are checked):
  calls       number of requests the fake received
  outcome     "ok" or "exception" (what the app saw)
  exception   exception class name, when outcome is "exception"
  tokens      per call: {"input": n, "output": n}, or None when the fake sent no usage
  finish      per call: finish/stop reason or response status
  tool_calls  per call: tool names the model asked for
  fake        per call: what the fake did (complete, failed, incomplete, error_event, cut, http_error)
  tool_runs   framework scenarios: each real tool run, {"name", "outcome": "ok" | "raised"}
  include_usage  per call: whether the app's own request asks for stream usage. When given,
              the comparer notes a request that carries include_usage the app did not ask for.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

from dataclasses import dataclass, field
from typing import Any

BUILT = "built"
NOT_BUILT = "not_built"

OA_TOK = {"input": 11, "output": 7}
AN_TOK = {"input": 5, "output": 3}


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Scenario:
    id: str
    provider: str  # openai, anthropic
    api: str  # chat, responses, messages
    framework: str  # none, langchain, langgraph, openai-agents
    does: str  # what the app does, in plain words
    app: str  # function name in trueup.runner.apps
    model: str  # fake scenario, sent as the model name
    expected: dict[str, Any] = field(default_factory=dict)
    status: str = BUILT

    @property
    def plain_sdk(self) -> bool:
        return self.framework == "none"

    def to_dict(self) -> dict[str, Any]:
        return {
            "id": self.id,
            "provider": self.provider,
            "api": self.api,
            "framework": self.framework,
            "does": self.does,
            "app": self.app,
            "model": self.model,
            "expected": self.expected,
            "status": self.status,
        }


def _ok(tokens: Any, finish: Any, tools: Any = None, calls: int = 1, fake: str = "complete") -> dict[str, Any]:
    return {
        "calls": calls,
        "outcome": "ok",
        "tokens": [tokens] * calls,
        "finish": [finish] * calls,
        "tool_calls": [tools or []] * calls,
        "fake": [fake] * calls,
    }


def _raises(exc: str, fake: str) -> dict[str, Any]:
    return {"calls": 1, "outcome": "exception", "exception": exc, "tokens": [None], "fake": [fake]}


def _s(id: str, provider: str, api: str, does: str, app: str, model: str, expected: dict[str, Any]) -> Scenario:
    return Scenario(id, provider, api, "none", does, app, model, expected)

from __future__ import annotations

import json
import time
from datetime import datetime, timezone
from pathlib import Path
from typing import Any, Callable

from trueup.core import report
from trueup.core.compare import compare, leads
from trueup.core.model import Mismatch, Observation
from trueup.runner import NOT_RUN, RAN, run_scenario, venvs
from trueup.runner.run import not_run

def new_run_id(library: str) -> str:
    return datetime.now(timezone.utc).strftime("%Y%m%dT%H%M%SZ") + f"-{library}"


def summary_line(r: dict[str, Any]) -> str:
    sid = r["scenario"]
    if r["status"] != RAN:
        return f"{sid:30} NOT RUN  {r['reason']}"
    t, tr = r["observation"]["truth"], r["observation"]["trace"]
    app = t["app"]["outcome"] if t["outcome"] == "ok" else f"raised {t['exception']}"
    spans = ", ".join(f"{s['name']}={s['status']['code']}" for s in tr["spans"]) or "none"
    line = f"{sid:30} ran {r['seconds']:5.1f}s  app {app}; fake calls {t['calls']}; spans {len(tr['spans'])}: {spans}"
    if t.get("expected_mismatch"):
        line += f"  [truth differs from scenario expectation: {', '.join(t['expected_mismatch'])}]"
    return line


def sweep(
    root: Path,
    library: str,
    framework: str = "all",
    *,
    ensure: Callable[[Path, str], Path] = venvs.ensure,
    run: Callable[..., dict[str, Any]] = run_scenario,
    out: Callable[[str], None] = print,
) -> tuple[Path, list[dict[str, Any]]]:
    run_id = new_run_id(library)
    run_dir = root / ".trueup" / "runs" / run_id
    run_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    started = time.monotonic()
    scenarios = select(framework)
    try:
        out(f"preparing venv for {library}")
        python: Path | None = ensure(root, library)
        venv_error = None
    except Exception as e:  # noqa: BLE001 - every scenario is reported NOT RUN
        python, venv_error = None, f"venv not ready: {e}"
    results = []
    for s in scenarios:
        r = not_run(s.id, library, venv_error) if python is None else run(python, library, s.id)
        if r["status"] == RAN:
            r["mismatches"] = [m.to_dict() for m in compare(Observation.from_dict(r["observation"]))]
        results.append(r)
        out(summary_line(r))
        (run_dir / f"{s.id}.json").write_text(json.dumps(r, indent=1, default=str))
    ran = sum(r["status"] == RAN for r in results)
    by = by_scenario(results)
    c = report.counts(by)
    table = report.table(by)
    totals = (f"leads: {c['leads']} (high {c['by_severity']['high']}, medium {c['by_severity']['medium']}, "
              f"low {c['by_severity']['low']})  notes: {c['notes']}")
    lines = [
        f"trueup sweep {library} --framework {framework}  run {run_id}",
        f"scenarios: {len(results)}  ran: {ran}  not run: {len(results) - ran}  "
        f"time: {time.monotonic() - started:.0f} s",
        totals,
        "A lead is a disagreement between truth and trace, not a confirmed bug.",
        "",
        *(summary_line(r) for r in results),
        "",
        table,
    ]
    (run_dir / "summary.txt").write_text("\n".join(lines) + "\n")
    (run_dir / "index.json").write_text(json.dumps({
        "run_id": run_id,
        "library": library,
        "framework": framework,
        "scenarios": [{"id": r["scenario"], "status": r["status"], "reason": r["reason"]} for r in results],
    }, indent=1))
    not_run_list = [{"scenario": r["scenario"], "reason": r["reason"]} for r in results if r["status"] != RAN]
    (run_dir / "leads.json").write_text(json.dumps(report.leads_payload(run_id, library, by, not_run_list), indent=1,
                                                   default=str))
    out("")
    out(table)
    out(totals)
    out(f"ran {ran}/{len(results)}; wrote {run_dir}")
    return run_dir, results


def by_scenario(results: list[dict[str, Any]]) -> list[tuple[str, list[Mismatch]]]:
    return [(r["scenario"], [Mismatch.from_dict(m) for m in r.get("mismatches", [])])
            for r in results if r["status"] == RAN]


def exit_code(results: list[dict[str, Any]]) -> int:
    """1 if any lead, else 2 if any scenario could not run, else 0."""
    if any(leads([m for _, ms in by_scenario(results) for m in ms])):
        return 1
    return 2 if not results or any(r["status"] == NOT_RUN for r in results) else 0

from __future__ import annotations

SRC = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[2]  # .../src

def child_env(base: dict[str, str] | None = None) -> dict[str, str]:
    env = dict(os.environ if base is None else base)
    for k in CHILD_ENV_DROP:
        env.pop(k, None)
    env.update(CHILD_ENV)
    env["PYTHONPATH"] = str(SRC)
    env.pop("VIRTUAL_ENV", None)
    return env


def not_run(scenario_id: str, library: str, reason: str, seconds: float = 0.0, detail: str | None = None) -> dict[str, Any]:
    return {"scenario": scenario_id, "library": library, "status": NOT_RUN, "reason": reason,
            "detail": detail, "seconds": round(seconds, 3), "observation": None}


def _last_line(text: str) -> str:
    lines = [ln for ln in text.strip().splitlines() if ln.strip()]
    return lines[-1].strip() if lines else "no output"


def run_scenario(python: Path, library: str, scenario_id: str, timeout: float = 90) -> dict[str, Any]:
    """Returns {scenario, library, status, reason, seconds, observation}."""
    try:
        scenario = get(scenario_id)
    except KeyError as e:
        return not_run(scenario_id, library, str(e))
    if scenario.status != BUILT:
        return not_run(scenario_id, library, f"scenario is {scenario.status}")
    return _run_child(python, library, scenario_id, [library, scenario_id], timeout)


def run_audit(python: Path, library: str, script: Path, label: str, overrides: dict[str, str],
              timeout: float = 90) -> dict[str, Any]:
    """Run a user's script's main() with the fake answering as `overrides` say. Same shape as run_scenario."""
    with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory(prefix="trueup-") as tmp:
        ov = Path(tmp) / "overrides.json"
        ov.write_text(json.dumps(overrides))
        return _run_child(python, library, label, ["--audit", library, str(script.resolve()), str(ov)], timeout)


def _run_child(python: Path, library: str, label: str, args: list[str], timeout: float) -> dict[str, Any]:
    with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory(prefix="trueup-") as tmp:
        out = Path(tmp) / "obs.json"
        cmd = [str(python), "-m", "trueup.runner.child", *args, str(out)]
        t0 = time.monotonic()
        try:
            p = subprocess.run(cmd, env=child_env(), cwd=tmp, capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=timeout)
        except subprocess.TimeoutExpired:
            return not_run(label, library, f"timed out after {timeout:.0f} s", time.monotonic() - t0)
        except OSError as e:
            return not_run(label, library, f"could not start {python}: {e}")
        seconds = time.monotonic() - t0
        if not out.exists():
            tail = (p.stderr or p.stdout).strip()[-2000:]
            return not_run(label, library, f"child exited {p.returncode} without output: {_last_line(tail)}",
                           seconds, detail=tail)
        payload = json.loads(out.read_text())
    if not payload["ok"]:
        return not_run(label, library, "setup or harness error: " + _last_line(payload["error"]), seconds,
                       detail=payload["error"])
    return {"scenario": label, "library": library, "status": RAN, "reason": None,
            "seconds": round(seconds, 3), "observation": payload["observation"]}

ATTR_MAX = 2000


def _value(v: Any) -> Any:
    if isinstance(v, (tuple, list)):
        return [_value(x) for x in v]
    if isinstance(v, str) and len(v) > ATTR_MAX:
        return v[:ATTR_MAX] + f"...[{len(v) - ATTR_MAX} more chars]"

def span_to_dict(s: Any) -> dict[str, Any]:
    ctx = s.get_span_context()
    return {
        "name": s.name,
        "kind": s.kind.name,
        "trace_id": format(ctx.trace_id, "032x"),
        "span_id": format(ctx.span_id, "016x"),
        "parent_id": format(s.parent.span_id, "016x") if s.parent else None,
        "start_ns": s.start_time,
        "end_ns": s.end_time,
        "status": {"code": s.status.status_code.name, "description": s.status.description},
        "scope": s.instrumentation_scope.name if s.instrumentation_scope else None,
        "attributes": {k: _value(v) for k, v in (s.attributes or {}).items()},
        "events": [{"name": e.name, "attributes": {k: _value(v) for k, v in (e.attributes or {}).items()}} for e in s.events],
    }


def _versions(library: str) -> dict[str, str | None]:
    out: dict[str, str | None] = {}
    for dist in VERSIONED[library]:
        try:
            out[dist] = metadata.version(dist)
        except metadata.PackageNotFoundError:
            out[dist] = None
    return out


def run(library: str, scenario_id: str) -> dict[str, Any]:
    scenario = get(scenario_id)
    logging.disable(logging.CRITICAL)
    exporter, flush = SETUPS[library](scenario.framework)
    check_framework(scenario.framework)
    if scenario.framework == "openai-agents":
        quiet_agents_sdk()
    app_fn = APPS[scenario.app]
    framework_apps.TOOL_RUNS.clear()
    with FakeProvider() as fake:
        t0 = time.monotonic()
        try:
            result = app_fn(fake.base_url, scenario.model)
            app = {"outcome": "ok", "result": result}
        except BaseException as e:  # noqa: BLE001 - the outcome is the data
            app = {
                "outcome": "exception",
                "exception_type": type(e).__name__,
                "exception_module": type(e).__module__,
                "message": str(e)[:500],
            }
        app["seconds"] = round(time.monotonic() - t0, 3)
        # Let streams closed by garbage collection end their spans.
        gc.collect()
        flush()
        fake_log = fake.log.entries()
    spans = [span_to_dict(s) for s in exporter.get_finished_spans()]
    t = truth.derive(fake_log, app, framework_apps.TOOL_RUNS)
    return {
        "truth": {
            **t,
            "scenario": scenario_id,
            "expected": scenario.expected,
            "expected_mismatch": truth.check_expected(scenario.expected, t),
            "app": app,
            "fake_log": fake_log,

    module = importlib.util.module_from_spec(spec)

    spec.loader.exec_module(module)
    fn = getattr(module, "main", None)
    if not callable(fn):
        raise AttributeError(f"{script} has no main()")

"""Trueup traces itself with neatlogs.

One trueup run = one neatlogs session (session id = run id). Each worker runs as
its own root trace named after it (trueup-planner, trueup-runner, ...), with
trueup.run_id, trueup.library and, where it applies, trueup.verdict.

This is the outer trace only. Scenario runs happen in subprocesses whose env
drops NEATLOGS_API_KEY and sets NEATLOGS_DISABLE_EXPORT / OTEL_*_EXPORTER=none
(trueup.runner.setups), so their spans never leave the machine.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import atexit
import contextlib
import os
import sys
from typing import Any, Callable, Iterator

from trueup import __version__

KEY_VAR = "NEATLOGS_API_KEY"
WORKERS = ("trueup-planner", "trueup-runner", "trueup-comparer", "trueup-checker", "trueup-deduper")

_state: dict[str, Any] = {"active": False, "run_id": None, "library": None, "flushed": False}


def active() -> bool:
    return bool(_state["active"])


def session_id() -> str | None:
    return _state["run_id"] if active() else None


def start(run_id: str, library: str, command: str, out: Callable[[str], None] = print,
          init: Callable[..., Any] | None = None) -> bool:
    """neatlogs.init for a command that calls the model. Returns whether tracing is on."""
    _state.update(active=False, run_id=run_id, library=library, flushed=False)
    if not os.environ.get(KEY_VAR):
        out(f"{KEY_VAR} is not set: running without neatlogs tracing")
        return False
    if init is None:
        import neatlogs

        init = neatlogs.init
    try:
        init(api_key=os.environ[KEY_VAR], workflow_name="trueup", instrumentations=["openai"],
             tags=[f"run_id:{run_id}", f"library:{library}", f"trueup:{__version__}", f"command:{command}"])
    except Exception as e:  # noqa: BLE001 - tracing must not stop the run
        out(f"neatlogs init failed ({type(e).__name__}): running without neatlogs tracing")
        return False
    _state["active"] = True
    atexit.register(flush)
    out(f"neatlogs tracing on, session {run_id}")
    return True


def flush() -> None:
    """Flush neatlogs once. Safe to call more than once and when tracing is off."""
    if not active() or _state["flushed"]:
        return
    _state["flushed"] = True
    try:
        import neatlogs

        neatlogs.flush()
    except Exception as e:  # noqa: BLE001
        print(f"neatlogs flush failed ({type(e).__name__})", file=sys.stderr)


@contextlib.contextmanager
def worker(name: str, **attrs: Any) -> Iterator[Any]:
    """A root trace for one worker in the run's session. Yields a span (or None when off)."""
    if name not in WORKERS:
        raise ValueError(f"unknown worker {name!r}")
    if not active():
        yield None
        return
    import neatlogs

    a = {"trueup.run_id": _state["run_id"], "trueup.library": _state["library"], "neatlogs.workflow.name": name,
         **{f"trueup.{k}": v for k, v in attrs.items()}}
    with neatlogs.trace(name=name, kind="AGENT", session_id=_state["run_id"], **a):
        from opentelemetry import trace as otel

        yield otel.get_current_span()


def set_verdict(span: Any, verdict: str) -> None:
    if span is not None:
        span.set_attribute("trueup.verdict", verdict)


def run_traced(run_id: str, library: str, command: str, body: Callable[[], int],
               out: Callable[[str], None] = print) -> int:
    """Start tracing, run the command, and flush on the way out, also when it raises."""
    start(run_id, library, command, out)
    try:
        return body()
    finally:
        flush()

"""trueup plan <library> [--max N]: the model proposes new scenarios as data; code decides.

The planner reads the library's wrapper source from its venv, the scenario
library and the latest findings, and asks the model for new scenarios as JSON.
Every proposal is checked by trueup.scenarios.proposed (schema, app and fake
behaviour exist, truth matches an untraced run). A rejected proposal goes back
to the model with the reason, at most REVISIONS times. Accepted ones are saved
to scenarios/proposed/<library>/ for `trueup sweep <library> --proposed`.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import json
from pathlib import Path
from typing import Any, Callable

from trueup import tracing
from trueup.model import PLAN_MODEL, ModelClient, ModelError, record_spend
from trueup.scenarios import ALL
from trueup.scenarios import proposed as prop

REVISIONS = 2
SOURCE_LIMIT = 60_000  # characters of wrapper source sent to the model
FILE_LIMIT = 32_000

# Wrapper files per library, relative to site-packages, most relevant first.
WRAPPER_FILES = {
    "neatlogs": ["neatlogs/openai.py", "neatlogs/anthropic.py"],
    "openllmetry": ["opentelemetry/instrumentation/openai/shared/chat_wrappers.py",
                    "opentelemetry/instrumentation/anthropic/streaming.py",
                    "opentelemetry/instrumentation/openai/v1/responses_wrappers.py"],
    "openinference": ["openinference/instrumentation/openai/_stream.py",
                      "openinference/instrumentation/openai/_request.py",
                      "openinference/instrumentation/anthropic/_stream.py"],
}

SYSTEM = """You plan test scenarios for Trueup, which checks whether an AI tracing library's spans match \
what really happened. A scenario runs one existing app function against a fake provider; the fake model name \
picks the fake's behaviour. You cannot write code: a scenario is JSON data that combines an existing app with an \
existing fake model, plus the truth you expect the run to produce.

Propose scenarios that are NEW (an app + fake model pair not already in the library) and likely to expose a \
tracing bug, given the wrapper source: code paths the existing scenarios miss (a different app reading style on \
the same failure, streaming vs non-streaming, async, tools with errors, refusal through streaming, ...).

Expected truth fields (only listed ones are checked, against what the fake really did):
  calls: number of requests the fake received
  outcome: "ok" or "exception" (what the app saw); exception: the exception class name when outcome is exception
  fake: per call, what the fake did: complete, failed, incomplete, error_event, cut, http_error
  tokens: per call {"input": n, "output": n}, or null when the fake sent no usage
  finish: per call, list of finish reasons / response status
  tool_calls: per call, list of tool names the model asked for
  tool_runs: framework apps only, [{"name", "outcome": "ok"|"raised"}]
  include_usage: per call, whether the app's request asked for stream usage
Facts about the fake: OpenAI replies use 11 input / 7 output tokens, Anthropic 5 / 3. Streams send usage only \
when the app asks (include_usage) on chat; Responses and Anthropic streams always send it. Leave out a field \
when unsure rather than guess; calls, outcome and fake are required.

Reply with JSON only, no prose: {"proposals": [{"id": "p-...", "provider", "api", "framework", "does", "app", \
"model", "expected": {...}, "rationale": "why a wrapper might get this wrong"}]}"""


def wrapper_source(root: Path, library: str) -> str:
    site = next((root / ".trueup" / "venvs" / library / "lib").glob("python*/site-packages"), None)
    if site is None:
        raise FileNotFoundError(f"no venv for {library}; run `trueup sweep {library}` first")
    parts, total = [], 0
    for rel in WRAPPER_FILES[library]:
        f = site / rel
        if not f.exists() or total >= SOURCE_LIMIT:
            continue
        text = f.read_text()[: min(FILE_LIMIT, SOURCE_LIMIT - total)]
        total += len(text)
        parts.append(f"### {rel}\n{text}")
    return "\n\n".join(parts)


def latest_findings(root: Path, library: str) -> list[dict[str, Any]]:
    runs = sorted((root / ".trueup" / "runs").glob(f"*-{library}/findings.json"))
    if not runs:
        return []
    d = json.loads(runs[-1].read_text())
    out = [{"title": f["title"], "severity": f["severity"], "check": f["details"]["check"],
            "scenarios": f["details"]["scenarios"]} for f in d["findings"]]
    out += [{"title": f.get("title"), "verdict": "disputed"} for f in d.get("disputed_semantics", [])]

def _plan(root: Path, library: str, max_n: int, client: ModelClient, result: dict[str, Any],
          out: Callable[[str], None], untraced: Callable[..., Any], save: bool) -> None:
    source = wrapper_source(root, library)
    findings = latest_findings(root, library)
    out(f"planning for {library}: {len(source)} chars of wrapper source, {len(findings)} findings")
    reply = client.chat_json(PLAN_MODEL, first_prompt(library, source, findings, max_n))
    props = reply.get("proposals") if isinstance(reply, dict) else None
    if not isinstance(props, list):
        raise ModelError('model reply has no "proposals" list; stopping the planner')
    existing = prop.load()
    taken = {(s.app, s.model) for s in existing}
    ids = {s.id for s in existing}
    for p in props[:max_n]:
        result["proposals"].append(p)
        pid = p.get("id", "?") if isinstance(p, dict) else "?"
        history = []
        for attempt in range(REVISIONS + 1):
            reasons = check(p, taken, ids, untraced)
            if not reasons:

            history.append({"proposal": p, "reasons": reasons})
            out(f"  {pid}: rejected ({'; '.join(reasons)[:200]})")
            if attempt == REVISIONS:
                break
            rev = client.chat_json(PLAN_MODEL, revision_prompt(p, reasons))
            revised = rev.get("proposals") if isinstance(rev, dict) else None
            if not revised:
                history.append({"proposal": None, "reasons": ["withdrawn by the model"]})
                reasons = ["withdrawn by the model after: " + "; ".join(reasons)]
                break
            p = revised[0]
        if reasons:
            result["rejected"].append({"id": pid, "reasons": reasons, "tries": len(history), "history": history})
            continue
        taken.add((p["app"], p["model"]))
        ids.add(p["id"])
        path = prop.save(p, library) if save else None
        result["accepted"].append({"id": p["id"], "revisions": len(history), "proposal": p,
                                   "path": str(path.relative_to(root)) if path else None})
        out(f"  {p['id']}: accepted{f' after {len(history)} revision(s)' if history else ''}")

import json

from types import SimpleNamespace

import openai
import pytest

from trueup import planner
from trueup.model import (CHEAP_MODEL, PLAN_MODEL, ModelClient, ModelError, SpendLimitReached, get_spend,
                          parse_json, proxy_root, record_spend)
from trueup.scenarios import get
from trueup.scenarios import proposed as prop
from trueup.sweep import sweep

GOOD = {
    "id": "p-chat-stream-usage-tools", "provider": "openai", "api": "chat", "framework": "none",
    "does": "Streams two tool calls with include_usage.", "app": "chat_stream_usage", "model": "chat-tools",
    "expected": {"calls": 1, "outcome": "ok", "fake": ["complete"], "tokens": [{"input": 11, "output": 7}],
                 "tool_calls": [["get_weather", "get_time"]]},
}


class FakeResp:
    def __init__(self, status=200, body=None):
        self.status_code, self._body = status, body

    def json(self):
        return self._body


def spend_get(spend, calls=None):
    def get(url, headers=None, timeout=None):
        if calls is not None:
            calls.append((url, headers))
        return FakeResp(200, {"info": {"spend": spend}})
    return get


class FakeOpenAI:
    """Stands in for openai.OpenAI: replies are strings, or exceptions to raise."""

    def __init__(self, replies):
        self.replies, self.sent = list(replies), []
        self.chat = SimpleNamespace(completions=SimpleNamespace(create=self._create))

    def _create(self, **kw):
        self.sent.append(kw)
        r = self.replies.pop(0)
        if isinstance(r, Exception):
            raise r
        usage = SimpleNamespace(prompt_tokens=100, completion_tokens=20)
        return SimpleNamespace(usage=usage, choices=[SimpleNamespace(message=SimpleNamespace(content=r))])


def client(replies, spend=0.0, calls=None):
    return ModelClient("k-test", "http://proxy.test/v1", http_get=spend_get(spend, calls),
                       openai_client=FakeOpenAI(replies), sleep=lambda s: None)


def conn_error():
    return openai.APIConnectionError(request=__import__("httpx").Request("POST", "http://proxy.test"))


# --- model client and spending guard


def test_proxy_root_strips_v1():
    assert proxy_root("https://p.example/v1/") == "https://p.example"
    assert proxy_root("https://p.example") == "https://p.example"


def test_guard_reads_key_info_with_bearer():
    calls = []
    assert get_spend("http://proxy.test/v1", "k-test", spend_get(3.5, calls)) == 3.5
    assert calls == [("http://proxy.test/key/info", {"Authorization": "Bearer k-test"})]


@pytest.mark.parametrize("spend", [15.0, 15.01, 99])
def test_guard_refuses_at_or_over_limit(spend):
    c = client(["{}"], spend=spend)
    with pytest.raises(SpendLimitReached, match="spend limit reached"):
        c.chat(PLAN_MODEL, [{"role": "user", "content": "hi"}])
    assert c.client.sent == []  # no model call made


def test_guard_allows_under_limit():
    c = client(['{"ok": 1}'], spend=14.99)
    assert c.chat_json(CHEAP_MODEL, [{"role": "user", "content": "hi"}]) == {"ok": 1}
    assert c.usage.calls == 1 and c.usage.input_tokens == 100

    c = ModelClient("k", "http://proxy.test/v1", http_get=lambda *a, **k: FakeResp(500),

    with pytest.raises(ModelError, match="HTTP 500"):
